question: This year, the Strategic Plan intervention measure ‘Conservation of endangered Lithuanian old breeds of livestock and poultry’ included the possibility of receiving support for keeping the European dark bee (Apis mellifera mellifera). Bees of different species are mixing rapidly.

Officially published research on the European dark bee in Lithuania has shown that of the 598 colonies surveyed in traditionally managed apiaries, only 52% contained part of the Apis mellifera mellifera gene. The question therefore arises as to how support will be granted to those who have genuine apiaries of the species in question. In the light of the foregoing: 1.

Has the Commission been informed of how, in this particular case, Lithuania will seek to avoid the possible erroneous granting of aid to apiaries which only have bees similar to or which share some characteristics of the European dark bee, but which do not actually belong to the Apis mellifera mellifera family and are such measures sufficient?

Can a beekeeper’s membership of the Lithuanian Dark Bee Association be considered a sufficient safeguard? Is it not contrary to EU law to single out one non-governmental association and grant preferential treatment to its members?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.6.

2024) The support provided through the agri-environment-climate intervention KP09gen Conservation of endangered Lithuanian old breeds of livestock and poultry, under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plan of Lithuania, can only be provided for farm animals of local endangered breeds which are recognised by the Member State in line with the provisions of Article 45(2)(a) of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1261.

It is the responsibility of the Member State to ensure the conditions for granting of support are respected, and these include the requirement for a duly recognised breed society to register and keep up to date the herd or flock breeding book for the breed in question.

According to the information provided in the CAP Strategic Plan of Lithuania, in the case of support for the Lithuanian dark bee (Apis mellifer melifera) this role is undertaken by the Association of the Lithuanian Dark Bees and there are 115 bee colonies registered in the flock breeding book for this breed which would therefore be eligible for support.
Accessing EU support is thus linked to registration of a bee colony in the breeding book for the species, rather than membership of an association.
